justification: Carrying span: 'Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment in any quarter when at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute, and has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters.' Taken in 23 of 24 => unpaid in exactly 1; 24 quarters = six years, so C is literally true. A dies on the same span: the test is a proportion of sailings inside a ten-minute window, not how far behind the booked minute the average sailing berths. B dies on 'Alison Bexwarden drafted the punctuality clause for the transport authority in 2011' set against 'in 2016 the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out' - the clause predates the withdrawal by five years. D dies on 'A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether' plus 'the crossing lost forty-one sailings to weather and a gearbox, and its reliability figure was ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been' - cancellations raise the figure, they do not reduce the payment.

Carrying span: 'He starts with 2005. The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking' - the printed eighteen minutes allowed less than the twenty-four the boat was taking, reinforced by 'the old seventy-one per cent measured a promise nobody could keep, and six of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat.' B dies on Cottam's own 'Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes... One boat gives you one every seventy' - seventy is now, twenty-five was 2005, and it is not unchanged. C dies for want of any loading claim: the only berthing-work span is 'The linkspan ... was rebuilt in 2013 ... its locking sequence takes a manufacturer's ninety seconds at each berth', which makes that work longer now, not longer then. D dies on 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005' - lateness was being measured in 2005.

Carrying span: Cottam's 'Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes... One boat gives you one every seventy. Pad the book by nothing at all and you'd still have that,' read against 'the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two' before the certificate ran out. The timetable changes account for 25->32; the lost boat accounts for 32->70, so the withdrawal removed more departures from the day than the timetable changes had. A dies on 'The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out' - padding came first. B dies for want of a span: the only stated reason is 'in 2016 the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her'; nothing ties the withdrawal to the linkspan. C dies on 'Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was' - the gap had already stretched 25->32, so the withdrawal was not what first stretched it.

Carrying span: 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing, and does not contest the fifteen minutes. Where Cattermay's case thins is the join.' Numbers granted, attribution withheld - and 'The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well' is the refusal of her cause. A dies on 'Nobody disputes the stamps' - the minutes are conceded, not shown to be little. C dies on 'the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well': the writer withholds the timetable's fault outright, not merely its magnitude. D dies on the same 'Nobody disputes the stamps' (no doubt about the numbers) and again on 'would bear either of the other two just as well' (no grant that the timetable is probably to blame).

Carrying span: the whole spine of the piece - 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005. Last year it was ninety-six' against 'The median time from barrier to far ramp has gone from thirty-nine minutes to fifty-four', with three named parties assigning the gap to different causes ('Something else happened in the middle of my series that I can't take apart yet'; 'the something else is nearly the whole of it'; 'does not accept that it caused any of this'). A dies on 'In the consultation that preceded it, sixty-one per cent of those answering ranked getting across sooner below knowing when the boat would go' - passengers were consulted. B dies on 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing' - there is no dispute over which source to believe. C dies on 'None of the three is arguing about the sentence Bexwarden raised herself' and 'That's the line I'd change ... and nobody writes to me about it' - there is no argument over renewing the clause; the draft carries it 'word for word'.

Backwards method - what each option would require the text to have said. A would require the payment test to be an average-lateness threshold; the text sets a proportion threshold, 'at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute'. Requirement violated. B would require the clause to date from the withdrawal; the text dates it to 2011 twice ('Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment'; 'drafted the punctuality clause ... in 2011') and the withdrawal to 2016. Violated. D would require a partial-reduction mechanic on cancellations; the text supplies the opposite mechanic - 'A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether' - and the worked example of forty-one lost sailings producing 'ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been'. Violated. C would require exactly one missed quarter inside twenty-four; 'has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters' supplies 24-23=1, and twenty-four quarters is six years. Requirement met, so C carries.

Backwards method. B would require Cottam to put 2005 departures seventy minutes apart and unchanged since; his own words put 2005 at twenty-five ('Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes') and seventy at present ('One boat gives you one every seventy'). Violated on both limbs. C would require a stated 2005 loading allowance and loading longer then than now; the text has no loading claim at all, and its nearest span makes berthing work newer and longer ('rebuilt in 2013 ... ninety seconds at each berth'). Unmet. D would require lateness to have gone unmeasured in 2005; 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005' supplies the measurement. Violated. A would require a 2005 booked figure below a 2005 actual figure; 'The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking' supplies exactly that, and 'six of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat' confirms the direction. Met, so A carries.

Backwards method. A would require the 2016 withdrawal to precede the first padding; 'The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out' reverses the order. Violated. B would require some stated linkspan-to-withdrawal link; the only reason given is 'the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her', and the linkspan appears in a separate sentence about axle loads. Unmet. C would require the withdrawal to be the first thing to stretch the departure interval; 'the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two' pre-2016, glossed as 'Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was'. Violated. D would require the two causes to be comparable in departures lost; the text supplies 25->32 for the timetable and 32->70 once the boat had gone, and Cottam's 'Pad the book by nothing at all and you'd still have that' makes the boat the dominant term. Met, so D carries.

Backwards method. A would require the writer to discount the fifteen minutes; 'Nobody disputes the stamps' and 'does not contest the fifteen minutes' refuse that. Violated. D would require doubt about her numbers; refused by the same span. Violated. C would require the writer to grant that the timetable is at fault while withholding only the size of the effect; the text withholds the fault itself - 'The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well' - so the reading she prefers is one of three live readings, not an established one. Violated. B would require numbers accepted and attribution refused; 'Nobody disputes the stamps' gives the first and 'Where Cattermay's case thins is the join ... she says herself that she cannot pull them apart' gives the second. Met, so B carries.

Backwards method. A would require an unconsulted-passenger strand; the text supplies a consultation with a published result - 'In the consultation that preceded it, sixty-one per cent of those answering ranked getting across sooner below knowing when the boat would go'. Violated. B would require a credibility contest between the reliability figure and the stamps; 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing' removes the contest, leaving a dispute about explanation rather than belief. Violated. C would require an argument about carrying the clause into the next contract; 'None of the three is arguing about the sentence Bexwarden raised herself', 'nobody writes to me about it', and a draft that 'carries the 2011 clause word for word' all refuse it. Violated. D would require an improved punctuality record, lengthened passenger journeys, and a live disagreement about the connection; the text supplies seventy-one to ninety-six per cent, thirty-nine to fifty-four minutes barrier-to-ramp, and three named parties assigning the gap differently. Met, so D carries.
